headline: Heavy Rainfall Causes Flooding Across Riverton
content:
Continuous rainfall began across Riverton late on August 13, causing
several streets in the eastern part of the city to flood by early Friday
morning. The city weather office recorded 118 millimetres of rain in
twelve hours.

Emergency services received their first major flooding calls at
approximately 5:30 a.m. on August 14. Water entered ground-floor homes
in the Riverside neighbourhood, and traffic was diverted from the Old
Bridge.

The municipal corporation opened two temporary shelters at Central High
School and the Riverside Community Hall. Officials said that 46
residents had been moved to the shelters by 10 a.m.

The weather office warned that further rainfall was expected through
Saturday. Residents were advised to avoid underpasses and roads near the
river.

headline: Schools Closed as Riverton River Level Rises
content:
Heavy rainfall continued in Riverton on Friday, August 14, leading
authorities to close all municipal schools for the day. The decision was
announced at 7:15 a.m. after water levels in the Riverton River rose
sharply overnight.

The Old Bridge was closed to vehicles at around 6 a.m. as a precaution.
Police redirected traffic toward the North Bypass, while emergency teams
helped residents leave low-lying homes in Riverside.

The municipal corporation confirmed that temporary shelters had been set
up at Central High School and Riverside Community Hall. By noon,
approximately 60 people were staying at the two locations.

The district collector said that a review meeting would be held at 4
p.m. to assess the situation. The weather office forecast more rain
until Saturday evening.

headline: Power Supply Restored in Parts of Flood-Hit Riverton
content:
Rainfall eased in Riverton on Saturday, August 15, but several
neighbourhoods continued to deal with flooding caused by the previous
day’s downpour. The weather office reported that the city had received
118 millimetres of rain in the twelve hours leading up to Friday
morning.

The municipal corporation said that 60 residents had used the temporary
shelters at Central High School and Riverside Community Hall. Officials
began distributing drinking water and food packets at both sites.

Power supply, which had been suspended in parts of Riverside as a safety
measure, was restored to most streets by 11 a.m. Repair crews continued
to inspect damaged electrical equipment.

The Old Bridge remained closed while engineers checked its structural
safety. The district collector said that a decision on reopening the
bridge would be made after the inspection. No deaths had been reported
as of Saturday afternoon.

headline: Temporary Shelters Open as Floodwater Enters Riverside Homes
content:
Floodwater entered ground-floor homes in the Riverside neighbourhood on
Friday morning after continuous rainfall overnight. Emergency teams
helped families leave low-lying streets before dawn.

The municipal corporation opened two temporary shelters at Central High
School and the Riverside Community Hall. Officials said that 46
residents had been moved to the shelters by 10 a.m.

Volunteers from nearby wards brought blankets, mats and cooked meals to
both locations. By noon, approximately 60 people were staying at the two
locations.

Police advised residents to stay away from the river bank and flooded
underpasses. The weather office said more rain was likely through
Saturday.

headline: Old Bridge Closed to Vehicles as Riverton River Swells
content:
The Old Bridge was closed to vehicles at around 6 a.m. as a precaution,
traffic police confirmed. Water in the Riverton River had risen sharply
overnight and was close to the bridge deck.

Police redirected traffic toward the North Bypass, which saw heavy
congestion through the morning. Buses on three city routes were rerouted
or cancelled.

Commuters were advised to avoid underpasses and roads near the river.
Several low-lying junctions in Riverside remained under water by noon.

Traffic officials said the bridge would stay closed until engineers
declared it safe. An update is expected after the review meeting on
Friday afternoon.

headline: Weather Office Warns Riverton of More Rain Through Saturday
content:
The city weather office recorded 118 millimetres of rain in twelve
hours, the highest twelve-hour total in Riverton this monsoon.
Continuous rainfall began late on August 13 and continued into Friday
morning.

The weather office warned that further rainfall was expected through
Saturday. Forecasters said a slow-moving system over the coast was
feeding the downpour.

Residents were advised to avoid underpasses and roads near the river.
Farmers on the outskirts were asked to delay harvesting until the rain
eased.

The Riverton River crossed its warning mark overnight, according to the
irrigation department. Officials said levels would be checked every two
hours.

headline: Collector Calls Review Meeting as Schools Shut in Riverton
content:
Authorities closed all municipal schools in Riverton on Friday, August
14, because of the flooding. The decision was announced at 7:15 a.m.
after water levels in the Riverton River rose sharply overnight.

The district collector said that a review meeting would be held at 4
p.m. to assess the situation. Senior officials from the municipal
corporation, the police and the weather office were asked to attend.

The municipal corporation confirmed that temporary shelters had been set
up at Central High School and Riverside Community Hall. Teams were also
checking pumping stations in the eastern part of the city.

Private schools were asked to follow the closure order. The education
department said exams scheduled for Friday would be rescheduled.

headline:
Review Meeting Orders Food and Water for Riverton Flood
Victims
content:
The district collector held a review meeting on Friday at 4 p.m. to
assess the flood situation in Riverton. Officials from the municipal
corporation, police and weather office attended.

The meeting directed the municipal corporation to distribute drinking
water and food packets at all shelters. It also ordered medical teams to
be stationed at Central High School and Riverside Community Hall.

Officials said approximately 60 people had stayed at the two shelters on
Friday. The collector asked ward officers to survey damaged homes once
the water recedes.

Engineers were told to inspect the Old Bridge before it is reopened. The
weather office forecast more rain until Saturday evening.

headline: Riverside Residents Return to Damaged Homes as Water Recedes
content:
Water began to recede from the Riverside neighbourhood on Saturday
morning as rainfall eased. Many families returned to find furniture and
household goods damaged by the flood.

The municipal corporation said that 60 residents had used the temporary
shelters at Central High School and Riverside Community Hall. Most of
them had returned home by Saturday evening, while those with unsafe
homes stayed on.

Power supply, which had been suspended in parts of Riverside as a safety
measure, was restored to most streets by 11 a.m. Residents said the
supply was steady through the afternoon.

Ward officers began recording damage to homes and shops. Families were
asked to keep photographs of the damage for compensation claims.

headline: Engineers Inspect Old Bridge as Riverton Waits to Reopen It
content:
The Old Bridge remained closed while engineers checked its structural
safety. A team from the public works department examined the pillars and
approach roads on Saturday.

The district collector said that a decision on reopening the bridge
would be made after the inspection. Officials expected a preliminary
report by Sunday morning.

No deaths had been reported as of Saturday afternoon. Two people were
treated for minor injuries after slipping on flooded roads.

Repair crews continued to inspect damaged electrical equipment. Traffic
continued to use the North Bypass, where police deployed extra
personnel.

headline: Riverton Schools Likely to Reopen on Monday, Officials Say
content:
Municipal schools in Riverton, which were closed on Friday, are likely
to reopen on Monday, the education department said. The final decision
depends on the weather and the condition of school buildings.

Central High School is being used as a temporary shelter and may need to
be vacated before classes resume. Officials said alternative
arrangements were being discussed.

Heavy rainfall continued in Riverton on Friday, August 14, leading
authorities to close all municipal schools for the day. Rainfall eased
on Saturday, but several neighbourhoods continued to deal with flooding.

Parents were asked to wait for an official announcement on Sunday
evening. Teachers have been asked to inspect classrooms on Sunday.

headline: Old Bridge Reopens to Light Vehicles After Inspection
content:
The Old Bridge in Riverton was reopened to light vehicles on Sunday
morning after engineers completed their inspection. Heavy vehicles and
buses remain barred until further tests are done.

The district collector said that the structure had not suffered serious
damage. Minor cracks in the approach road were repaired overnight.

Police removed the diversion toward the North Bypass for cars and
two-wheelers. Traffic officers will monitor water levels in the Riverton
River throughout the day.

Bus services on three routes resumed on Sunday afternoon using the North
Bypass. Officials said normal bus movement over the bridge would be
allowed after a load test.

headline: Schools Reopening Delayed as Riverton Shelter Stays Open
content:
The education department said that municipal schools in Riverton will
now reopen on Tuesday instead of Monday. Central High School is still
being used as a temporary shelter.

Officials said that 28 residents whose homes remain unsafe are still
staying at the shelter. The remaining families have moved back to
Riverside or to relatives' homes.

The municipal corporation said it would shift those residents to the
Riverside Community Hall by Monday evening. Classrooms at Central High
School will then be cleaned and disinfected.

Parents expressed concern about missed lessons. The department said
extra classes would be arranged later in the month.

headline: Power Restored to All Riverside Streets After Flood Repairs
content:
Power supply was restored to the remaining streets of Riverside on
Sunday, the electricity board said. Repair crews had finished inspecting
damaged electrical equipment late on Saturday.

Power supply, which had been suspended in parts of Riverside as a safety
measure, was restored to most streets by 11 a.m. on Saturday. The
remaining streets needed new cables after water damaged a transformer.

Engineers replaced one transformer and four street-level junction boxes.
The electricity board said it had deployed 12 repair crews across the
eastern part of the city.

Residents were asked not to touch wires or switches in flooded homes
until they are checked. A helpline was opened for complaints.

headline:
Health Officials Warn of Waterborne Disease After Riverton
Floods
content:
Health officials in Riverton warned residents of waterborne diseases
after the flooding. No outbreak had been reported as of Sunday, but
doctors expect cases of diarrhoea and fever to rise.

Medical teams were stationed at Central High School and the Riverside
Community Hall, as ordered at the Friday review meeting. Chlorine
tablets were distributed in flooded neighbourhoods.

Residents were advised to boil drinking water and avoid walking through
standing water. Officials began distributing drinking water and food
packets at both sites.

Mosquito control teams will begin fogging in Riverside on Monday. Health
officials asked people with fever to visit the nearest clinic.

headline: Riverton Counts the Cost of Flood Damage to Homes and Shops
content:
An initial survey by the municipal corporation found that 312 homes were
damaged in the Riverton floods. Dozens of shops in the eastern part of
the city also reported stock losses.

The corporation put the first estimate of damage at 40 crore rupees.
Officials said the figure could change as the survey continues.

Continuous rainfall began across Riverton late on August 13, causing
several streets in the eastern part of the city to flood by early Friday
morning. The city weather office recorded 118 millimetres of rain in
twelve hours.

Traders said they were waiting for insurance assessors to visit. The
chamber of commerce asked the state government for a relief package.

headline: Relief Work Continues at Riverton Shelters
content:
Relief work continued on Monday at the shelters set up after the
Riverton floods. Officials said 28 residents were still staying at
Central High School.

The municipal corporation moved these residents to the Riverside
Community Hall on Monday evening so that the school can be cleaned.
Volunteers helped carry belongings and bedding.

Drinking water, food packets and medicines were available at the hall
round the clock. Doctors visited twice a day to check on elderly
residents.

The district collector visited the hall and spoke to affected families.
He said that compensation forms would be issued within the week.

headline: Riverton Schools Reopen After Flood Closure
content:
Municipal schools in Riverton reopened on Tuesday, August 18, after
remaining closed since the floods. Classes at Central High School
resumed after the building was cleaned and disinfected.

Attendance was low on the first day, with many students still dealing
with damage at home. Teachers said they would not hold tests this week.

Heavy rainfall continued in Riverton on Friday, August 14, leading
authorities to close all municipal schools for the day. The closure was
extended over the weekend and into Monday as shelters remained in use.

The education department said that missed lessons would be covered
through extra classes. Students who lost books were offered free
replacements.
